title: qdrant xpcproxy stuck after kickstart cycle, needs KeepAlive in plist
description:
After the 2026-07-29 03:00 diagnostic recipe hammered qdrant with add+search across an hour of /learn captures, qdrant filled its open-file limit at ~652/1048576 and RocksDB failed every flush with "Too many open files" (RocksDB .log append). The Stop hook + a Memory.add() then timed out with qdrant_client.http.exceptions.ResponseHandlingException: timed out.

Attempted recovery path: launchctl kickstart -k ai.hermes.qdrant. Result: xpcproxy holds the slot, but launchd never spawns the qdrant child because the post-kickstart transition is stuck at "immediate reason = speculative, last exit code = (never exited)". Bootout+bootstrap returns "Bad request" because the wedged xpcproxy is already in the slot, and xpcproxy (pid 50465 / 79200) cannot be SIGKILL-ed by the user (bears jleechan_session but managed by launchd).

Root cause: the disk_magician-installed ai.hermes.qdrant.plist lacks a KeepAlive directive, so when a transient error forces qdrant into the half-spawn state, launchd cannot recover. The original platform script (start-qdrant-container.sh) had bash as PID 1 returning "docker not ready", which launchd would mark exit-coded and respawn next-tick.

Fix: add the keys KeepAlive (with SuccessfulExit: false) and ThrottleInterval: 5 to the plist. SuccessfulExit:false forces a respawn on any non-zero OR on signal-ish exits; ThrottleInterval:5 caps retry rate so we never stampede launchd.

Workaround (lossy): run qdrant via launchctl print-disable + direct user-level launch. Loses login-cycle durability but recovers read/write API now.

Live attempts recorded on 2026-07-29:
  kickstart -k → xpcproxy stays, qdrant child never spawns
  bootout then bootstrap → "Bad request" / already in slot
  kill -9 50465 → "Operation not permitted" (launchd-owned process)
  wait past exit-timeout=5s → still wedged at 5s
Recovery not yet achieved as of 2026-07-29 03:30 PDT. Outstanding.

Qdrant on localhost:6333 is currently down; recent writes (this /learn captures disk-full-2026-07-29 fact, plus the smaller earlier entries from this session) are at risk of being lost unless recovered.
notes:
RESOLVED 2026-07-29 02:01 PDT via /sidekick (mission disk_magician-o5v).

Root cause was three-fold, NOT just a missing KeepAlive:

1. The plist (added 2026-07-27) pointed qdrant at
   ~/.local/share/qdrant/storage but the live data was at
   ~/.hermes/qdrant_storage/ (redirected by the backup cron at
   some point; the migration was never propagated to the cron).
   The binary was coming up against an empty storage tree, holding
   the bind open until launchd classified the start as
   'speculative'.

2. The plist had no KeepAlive / ThrottleInterval. After my
   launchctl kickstart -k cycle, launchd could not recover.

3. ProcessType was Background. Even AFTER (1) and (2) were
   fixed, launchd SIGTERM'd the qdrant child at 09:10:40, 36s
   after first bind. This was the session-context reaper killing
   Background processes when the spawning shell exits. THIS IS THE
   DEEPEST BUG: KeepAlive's SuccessfulExit:false does NOT prevent
   Background reaping.

The fix that worked: ProcessType: Background -> Interactive
(processType change in plist, then launchctl bootstrap). After
the change qdrant pid 30212 is alive, /healthz is green, mem0
add+search both return successfully.

LESSON (memory bead linked): ProcessType Background on
user-scope launchd jobs is incompatible with keeping daemon-like
services alive across session boundaries. For a long-lived local
daemon (qdrant, mem0 hooks, etc.) ProcessType must be Interactive.

OUTSTANDING (related, deferred): the backup cron
ai.hermes.schedule.qdrant-backup.plist reads from
~/.hermes/qdrant_storage/ (old path) — its backups will be empty
until the cron path is updated to match the plist's path. Tracked
in the same bead as a follow-up.

draft, both flagged the same defect):** the original draft had `agent_worktree_create` allocate the
worktree parent via `agent_scratch_create "worktrees" ...`, nesting it inside
`/private/tmp/agent-scratch/<runtime>/<run-id>/worktrees/...`. That is a real safety bug, not a
style nit: that whole subtree is (a) subject to bead B4/`scratch_budget.sh`'s size-budget+age
eviction once enabled (bead i2o) and (b) removed wholesale by the A3 Stop hook
(`agent_scratch_cleanup_hook.sh`) when a session ends — neither check is worktree-aware, so either

"Worktree 7-day rule (hard)"'s protected window. Fixed by NOT reusing `agent_scratch_create`/the
agent-scratch root at all: worktrees get their own sibling root,
`/private/var/tmp/agent-worktrees/<label>-$$-$(date +%s)`, plain `mkdir -p`, never touched by
`scratch_budget.sh` eviction or the Stop hook (neither's root list includes
`/private/var/tmp/agent-worktrees`, and this bead's IMPL pair must not add it there). This trades away

was unsafe for worktrees. Cleanup of `/private/var/tmp/agent-worktrees` is explicitly NOT scoped to this
bead pair (a follow-up bead, not created here, would extend the existing 7-day-floor

regression this bead pair needs to close.

first `/private/tmp/agent-worktrees` choice was still unsafe**, even after removing the
`agent_scratch_create` nesting — `/private/tmp` itself (not just the agent-scratch subtree inside
it) is scanned one level deep by `cleanup_tmp.sh --large`, which runs in production TODAY (called by
`pressure_sweep.sh` with no dependency on bead i2o) and would archive-then-purge a top-level
`agent-worktrees` container after ~4h of no file changes anywhere under it (confirmed live:

sweeper in this repo scans `/private/var/tmp` at all. This is the actual fix; do not move the

test proving both `cleanup_tmp.sh --large` and `scratch_budget_evict_root` skip it.

Add `tests/test_agent_worktree.sh` proving a not-yet-created `scripts/lib/agent_worktree.sh`
provides `agent_worktree_create <label> <ref> <repo>` — allocates a managed leaf directory directly under
`AGENT_WORKTREE_ROOT` (env-overridable; defaults to `/private/var/tmp/agent-worktrees`; validates

## Goal

Depends on: T6-TEST closed. Line budget: ~35 new lines. Explicitly out of scope: registering this as a Claude Code Stop/SessionEnd hook in ~/.claude/settings.json — that requires separate, explicit user approval (global user config outside this repo's ownership) and is not part of this bead.

## Reuse
scripts/lib/agent_scratch.sh (T5-IMPL) — source it for the `AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT` default and the same `_agent_scratch_valid_component` validation logic this hook must apply to its own runtime/run-id inputs, so both accept/reject the same component shapes.

## Steps
1. Run: `test -f scripts/lib/agent_scratch.sh && echo EXISTS || echo MISSING` (expect `EXISTS`; confirms T5-IMPL has landed).
2. Create scripts/agent_scratch_cleanup_hook.sh with this exact content, then `chmod +x scripts/agent_scratch_cleanup_hook.sh`:
```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# agent_scratch_cleanup_hook.sh — removes exactly one leaf scratch dir
# ($AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT/<runtime>/<run-id>) on session end. Refuses to run
# without both identifying env vars, and refuses to ever touch
# $AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT itself. NOT wired into any hook config by this
# script — registration into ~/.claude/settings.json is a separate,
# approval-gated step (bead disk_magician-d45, spec section A3).
set -euo pipefail
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=scripts/lib/agent_scratch.sh
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/agent_scratch.sh"

if [[ -z "${AGENT_SCRATCH_RUNTIME:-}" || -z "${AGENT_SCRATCH_RUN_ID:-}" ]]; then
  echo "agent_scratch_cleanup_hook: refusing — AGENT_SCRATCH_RUNTIME and AGENT_SCRATCH_RUN_ID must both be set" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# Reuse the same component validator agent_scratch_create() applies (empty,
# path-traversal, and absolute/multi-segment components are all rejected) —
# an unvalidated runtime/run-id here would let a caller pass e.g.
# AGENT_SCRATCH_RUNTIME="../../.." and rm -rf outside AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT.
if ! _agent_scratch_valid_component "$AGENT_SCRATCH_RUNTIME"; then
  echo "agent_scratch_cleanup_hook: refusing — AGENT_SCRATCH_RUNTIME is not a valid single path component" >&2
  exit 1
fi
if ! _agent_scratch_valid_component "$AGENT_SCRATCH_RUN_ID"; then
  echo "agent_scratch_cleanup_hook: refusing — AGENT_SCRATCH_RUN_ID is not a valid single path component" >&2
  exit 1
fi

leaf="${AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT}/${AGENT_SCRATCH_RUNTIME}/${AGENT_SCRATCH_RUN_ID}"
if [[ "$leaf" == "$AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT" || "$leaf" == "$AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT/" ]]; then
  echo "agent_scratch_cleanup_hook: refusing — resolved path equals AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT itself" >&2
  exit 1
fi

rm -rf "$leaf"
```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# shellcheck shell=bash
# agent_scratch.sh — managed scratch root for agent runtimes (bead
# disk_magician-d45 producer-side prevention: namespaced runtime/run-id
# subtree under $AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT so budget eviction and a future
# Stop-hook cleanup script can target exactly a session's own scratch,
# without touching unrelated $TMPDIR entries left by other tools).
AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT="${AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT:-/private/tmp/agent-scratch}"

_agent_scratch_valid_component() {
  # Reject empty, path-traversal, and absolute-path / multi-segment components.
  local c="$1"
  [[ -n "$c" && "$c" != *".."* && "$c" != /* && "$c" != *"/"* ]]
}

agent_scratch_create() {
  local runtime="$1" run_id="$2"
  _agent_scratch_valid_component "$runtime" || { echo "agent_scratch_create: invalid runtime" >&2; return 1; }
  _agent_scratch_valid_component "$run_id" || { echo "agent_scratch_create: invalid run-id" >&2; return 1; }
  local path="${AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT}/${runtime}/${run_id}"
  mkdir -p "$path"
  echo "$path"
}

agent_scratch_trap_cleanup() {
  # Containment check (round-3 /advice hardening): refuse to arm cleanup
  # unless the caller-supplied path canonicalizes (symlinks resolved) to a
  # genuine leaf strictly under AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT/<runtime>/ — i.e. at
  # least two path segments below the canonicalized root, never the root
  # itself and never a bare <runtime> directory. This stops both a
  # symlink escape and an accidental "delete a whole runtime's scratch"
  # call.
  local path="$1" canon_root canon_path
  canon_root="$(cd "$AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)" || {
    echo "agent_scratch_trap_cleanup: AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT does not exist, refusing: $AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT" >&2
    return 1
  }
  if [[ ! -d "$path" ]]; then
    echo "agent_scratch_trap_cleanup: path does not exist, refusing: $path" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  canon_path="$(cd "$path" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)" || {
    echo "agent_scratch_trap_cleanup: cannot canonicalize path, refusing: $path" >&2
    return 1
  }
  case "$canon_path" in
    "$canon_root"/*/*) ;;
    *)
      echo "agent_scratch_trap_cleanup: refusing — $canon_path is not a leaf strictly under $canon_root/<runtime>/" >&2
      return 1
      ;;
  esac

  # Preserve each of EXIT/INT/TERM's own pre-existing handler individually
  # (a caller may have set different handlers per signal) — setting one
  # combined trap string for all three signals, using only EXIT's prior
  # handler text, would silently drop a caller's own INT/TERM handlers.
  # Escape embedded single quotes in canon_path (round-3 /advice hardening
  # -- a filename containing "'" would otherwise break out of the quoted
  # rm -rf argument when interpolated into the trap command string).
  local sig existing escaped_path
  escaped_path="${canon_path//\'/\'\\\'\'}"
  for sig in EXIT INT TERM; do
    existing="$(trap -p "$sig" | sed -E "s/^trap -- '(.*)' (SIG)?${sig}\$/\1/")"
    if [[ "$sig" == "EXIT" ]]; then
      trap "rm -rf '${escaped_path}'; ${existing}" "$sig"
    else
      # INT/TERM (round-3 /advice hardening): after cleanup + any prior
      # handler, re-raise the signal against ourselves with default
      # disposition restored, so the process actually terminates as the
      # caller expects on Ctrl-C/kill instead of silently continuing past
      # the now-deleted directory.
      trap "rm -rf '${escaped_path}'; ${existing:+${existing}; }trap - ${sig}; kill -s ${sig} \$BASHPID" "$sig"
    fi
  done
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# test_agent_scratch.sh — Behavioral tests for scripts/lib/agent_scratch.sh
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
LIB="$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/agent_scratch.sh"

FAKE_ROOT="$(mktemp -d -t agent_scratch_test.XXXXXX)"
export AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT="$FAKE_ROOT"

PASS=0
FAIL=0
record_pass() { echo "  PASS  $1"; PASS=$(( PASS + 1 )); }
record_fail() { echo "  FAIL  $1"; FAIL=$(( FAIL + 1 )); }

# shellcheck source=scripts/lib/agent_scratch.sh
source "$LIB"

path=$(agent_scratch_create "testruntime" "run123")
if [[ -d "$path" ]]; then record_pass "scratch dir created"; else record_fail "scratch dir not created"; fi
if [[ "$path" == "$FAKE_ROOT/testruntime/run123" ]]; then record_pass "correct path shape"; else record_fail "wrong path shape: $path"; fi

if agent_scratch_create "" "run123" 2>/dev/null; then record_fail "empty runtime accepted"; else record_pass "empty runtime rejected"; fi
if agent_scratch_create "testruntime" "../escape" 2>/dev/null; then record_fail "traversal accepted"; else record_pass "traversal rejected"; fi
if agent_scratch_create "testruntime" "/abs" 2>/dev/null; then record_fail "absolute run-id accepted"; else record_pass "absolute run-id rejected"; fi

(
  trap 'echo caller-trap-ran > "'"$FAKE_ROOT"'/caller_trap_marker"' EXIT
  agent_scratch_trap_cleanup "$path"
  exit 0
)
if [[ -f "$FAKE_ROOT/caller_trap_marker" ]]; then record_pass "caller's own EXIT trap still ran (chained, not clobbered)"; else record_fail "caller's own EXIT trap was overwritten"; fi
if [[ ! -d "$path" ]]; then record_pass "trap cleanup removed the scratch dir"; else record_fail "trap cleanup did not remove the scratch dir"; fi

# a correct implementation must preserve each signal's own prior handler,
# not just re-apply EXIT's handler text to all three signals.
path2=$(agent_scratch_create "testruntime" "run789")
(
  trap 'echo exit-trap-ran > "'"$FAKE_ROOT"'/exit_marker"' EXIT
  trap 'echo int-trap-ran > "'"$FAKE_ROOT"'/int_marker"' INT
  agent_scratch_trap_cleanup "$path2"
  kill -INT $BASHPID
  echo "unreachable" > "$FAKE_ROOT/unreachable_marker"
)
if [[ -f "$FAKE_ROOT/int_marker" ]]; then record_pass "caller's own INT trap still ran (preserved, not overwritten by EXIT's handler)"; else record_fail "caller's own INT trap was lost"; fi
if [[ -f "$FAKE_ROOT/unreachable_marker" ]]; then record_fail "subshell kept running after INT instead of terminating (signal re-raise is missing)"; else record_pass "subshell actually terminated on INT (signal correctly re-raised, not swallowed)"; fi

# Containment check: agent_scratch_trap_cleanup must independently refuse
# to arm cleanup on a path that is not a genuine leaf strictly under
# AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT/<runtime>/ — even if the caller bypasses
# agent_scratch_create and hand-constructs a bad path.
outside_dir="$(mktemp -d -t agent_scratch_outside.XXXXXX)"
if (AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT="$FAKE_ROOT" agent_scratch_trap_cleanup "$outside_dir" 2>/dev/null); then
  record_fail "trap_cleanup accepted a path entirely outside AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT"
else
  record_pass "trap_cleanup rejects a path entirely outside AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT"
fi
[[ -d "$outside_dir" ]] && record_pass "outside-root dir was never deleted" || record_fail "outside-root dir was deleted"
rm -rf "$outside_dir"

if (AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT="$FAKE_ROOT" agent_scratch_trap_cleanup "$FAKE_ROOT" 2>/dev/null); then
  record_fail "trap_cleanup accepted AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT itself"
else
  record_pass "trap_cleanup rejects AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT itself"
fi

mkdir -p "$FAKE_ROOT/bareruntime"
if (AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT="$FAKE_ROOT" agent_scratch_trap_cleanup "$FAKE_ROOT/bareruntime" 2>/dev/null); then
  record_fail "trap_cleanup accepted a bare <runtime> dir (only one segment below root)"
else
  record_pass "trap_cleanup rejects a bare <runtime> dir (only one segment below root)"
fi

# Round-3 /advice hardening: a leaf path containing a literal single quote
# must not break the quoted rm -rf interpolation inside the trap string.
quote_leaf=$(agent_scratch_create "testruntime" "run_with_quote")
mv "$quote_leaf" "${quote_leaf}o'clock" 2>/dev/null || true
if [[ -d "${quote_leaf}o'clock" ]]; then
  (
    trap 'true' EXIT
    agent_scratch_trap_cleanup "${quote_leaf}o'clock"
    exit 0
  )
  if [[ ! -d "${quote_leaf}o'clock" ]]; then
    record_pass "trap_cleanup correctly removes a leaf path containing a single quote"
  else
    record_fail "trap_cleanup left a quote-containing leaf path in place"
  fi
else
  record_fail "test setup could not create a quote-containing fixture path (filesystem may not support it)"
fi

rm -rf "$FAKE_ROOT"

echo ""
echo "Results: $PASS passed, $FAIL failed"
if (( FAIL > 0 )); then
  exit 1
fi
echo "All agent_scratch tests passed."

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# test_disk_diagnostic_scratch.sh — proves disk_diagnostic.sh's WORK dir is

  record_fail "disk_diagnostic.sh still allocates WORK via a bare mktemp, not agent_scratch_create"

  record_pass "disk_diagnostic.sh calls agent_scratch_create with runtime=disk_diagnostic"

  record_pass "disk_diagnostic.sh calls agent_scratch_trap_cleanup instead of a bare EXIT trap"
else
  record_fail "disk_diagnostic.sh does not call agent_scratch_trap_cleanup"
fi

rm -rf "$FAKE_ROOT"

echo ""
echo "Results: $PASS passed, $FAIL failed"
if (( FAIL > 0 )); then

fi
echo "All disk_diagnostic_scratch tests passed."

title: check_version_monotonic.py: current PR's own intra-branch version oscillation (bump-then-lower before merge) is not scanned — by design, non-blocking
description:
Codex /advice review on PR #73 (a0e3ace4853504abac7000783fe6c1028c957a25) flagged that get_git_log_versions() only walks <base_ref> --first-parent history, not the current branch's own commits since diverging from base. So a PR that bumps pyproject.toml's version then lowers it again in a later commit, all before merge, is not caught mid-review — only the final committed state is compared against base's own historical max.

This is a deliberate design choice (see PR #73 Tenets: 'No version bump in this PR unless the gate requires it' + 'CI uses origin/main as the authoritative tip'): the gate protects main's own linear version history, not intra-PR hygiene. The final merged state is what matters for 'version never regresses vs git history' — main's own first-parent history after merge is unaffected by transient intra-PR fluctuation. Reviewer Opus independently confirmed merge commits and origin/main/tag regressions are still caught.

If this class of intra-PR self-correction is ever judged worth blocking (e.g. to discourage version-bump churn in PR review), extend get_git_log_versions() to also scan '<base_ref>..HEAD --first-parent -p -- pyproject.toml' and union those versions in. Not urgent; tracked as a documented scope decision, not a regression.

pattern across scripts/).

title: fix: path_size_kb() breaks on multi-line du output during real $TMPDIR scan
description:
## Environment
Repo root: /Users/jleechan/projects_other/disk_magician, branch main. Bash. No throwaway worktree required.

## Found by
PR #71 (feat/scratch-size-budget) evidence run: real timed `bash scripts/cleanup_tmp.sh --dry-run --budget-gb 15` against the actual live $TMPDIR/DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR on a busy multi-agent dev box produced this non-fatal stderr during the DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR scan pass:

```
scripts/lib/scratch_budget.sh: line 143: 0
0: arithmetic syntax error in expression (error token is "0")
```

Script still exited 0 and completed (DRY RUN, no deletions attempted regardless). The failing line is `total_kb=$(( total_kb + kb ))` in `scratch_budget_evict_root()` (scripts/lib/scratch_budget.sh:143), fed by `kb=$(path_size_kb "$item")`.

## Root cause
`path_size_kb()` (scripts/cleanup_tmp.sh:217-219, pre-existing since 2026-06-09 commit 3bcaa23, NOT modified by PR #71):
```bash
path_size_kb() {
  du -sk "$1" 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1+0}' || echo 0
}
```
assumes `du -sk` always emits exactly one line to stdout. On a live, churning $TMPDIR this assumption breaks under TOCTOU races and BSD-du edge cases (confirmed empirically: `du -sk` on a path that vanishes mid-scan or is TCC-protected — e.g. `TemporaryItems` — emits ZERO lines to stdout, not one). Two-line output (each line evaluating to `0` via `$1+0`) produces `kb="0\n0"`, which breaks the downstream bash arithmetic at scratch_budget.sh:143.

This is pre-existing code, but PR #71's `scratch_budget_evict_root()` is the first caller to run `path_size_kb()` across *every* top-level entry of the full $TMPDIR/DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR root (existing callers apply it to a narrower, more curated candidate set), so it's the first code path to reliably surface this.

## Impact
Non-fatal, fails toward UNDER-counting (`total_kb` undercounted for the one racy item → budget eviction may under-trigger, never over-trigger). No data-loss risk. Does not block PR #71: the bug is in unmodified shared code, and PR #71's dry-run/`--budget-gb` path degrades safely through it (RC=0, correct dry-run summary still printed).

## Goal
Harden `path_size_kb()` in scripts/cleanup_tmp.sh (and its src/disk_magician/ mirror via sync_package_tree.sh) to tolerate non-single-line `du` output:
```bash
path_size_kb() {
  du -sk "$1" 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR==1{print $1+0; found=1} END{if(!found) print 0}'
}
```
(or equivalent `tail -1`/`head -1` guard). Add a regression test that stubs `du` to emit 2+ lines for one candidate and asserts `scratch_budget_evict_root`'s total_kb arithmetic does not error.

## Acceptance criteria
- `path_size_kb()` never causes an arithmetic error in any caller regardless of `du`'s line count.
- New/extended test in tests/test_scratch_budget.sh or tests/test_cleanup_safety.sh reproduces multi-line du output via a stub and proves no arithmetic error.
- `bash scripts/sync_package_tree.sh --check` clean after the src/ mirror update.

title: prune_aside_sessions.py: dedup_static_assets can hardlink messages.jsonl across a live in-use session
description: Found by Opus in /advice review of PR #59 (2026-09-01). dedup_static_assets() operates on retained_dirs, which explicitly includes sessions retained BECAUSE lsof reported them in-use (prune_aside_sessions.py, get_open_session_paths retained set). It hardlinks any regular file >=1KB with no static-asset filter, including messages.jsonl -- the most common >=1KB file in the real ~/.aside/u/*/sessions/ tree and one a live session actively appends to. Two byte-identical logs can get merged onto one inode, cross-contaminating a live session's log with another session's. Separately: the batch lsof parser (get_open_session_paths) uses line.split(None, 8) which silently drops any lsof output row with fewer than 9 whitespace-separated fields, letting an open session slip through undetected despite the function's fail-closed docstring. Fix: exclude retained_dirs (or specifically messages.jsonl / any actively-appended log) from dedup candidates, and harden the lsof line parser to fail closed on any row it cannot fully parse rather than silently skipping it.

title: Identify hidden daemon/launchd job writing to ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain (sawtooth broken since 2026-08-17)
description:
Found during disk-attribution 2026-08-20: ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain grew from sawtooth envelope of 2.5-13 GB to 38.7 GB over 3 days. Lane A verified: 592,475 files modified in last 7 days; recent transcript.jsonl / task-NNN.log files dated today; ps aux shows NO antigravity CLI but brain keeps growing. Top 5 subdirs of brain are session/state UUIDs totaling 31G (17G, 6.1G, 3.2G, 2.7G, 2.0G). Two-step fix needed:

(1) Identify the writer. Likely candidates: a launchd job not matching 'antigravity' in name (e.g. something under com.google.* or ai.google.* or a service account-owned process); or a parent daemon (e.g. NRD.UpdateBrainService-adjacent — though that one is Apple's, not antigravity's). Use: ps aux | grep -iE 'brain|gemini' ; launchctl list | grep -iE 'gemini|brain|antigravity|nrd'; lsof +D ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain 2>/dev/null | head.

(2) Once identified, decide: stop/restart the writer cleanly (so its GC fires and trims brain back to its 2.5-13 GB envelope); or, if writer can't be controlled, file an upstream bug with antigravity and put a temporary launchd watchdog in place.

Until (1) is done, do NOT delete brain contents — the writer will just regenerate. Full writeup: ~/roadmap/disk_magician/sidekick/disk-attr-aug-2026/LANE-A.md
